title: Photograph Before You Fix
subtitle: Your eye made peace with the mess months ago. The camera never did. Record an honest starting point before you change a thing.
hands_off_to: Chapter 7 (Define the Purpose of the Area)
audience: Readers who have chosen and audited a target space and are about to fix it. Busy home keepers and parents. New to applying the method. Some are camera-shy or privacy-conscious about their home.
core_promise: Record an honest before photo of your audited space, understand why your eye stopped seeing the mess, and learn to shoot a matched pair so the after lines up and proves the change.
emotional_purpose: Reassurance and future pride. Replace the embarrassment of photographing a mess with the understanding that the honest before is what makes the after feel earned, while respecting the reader's privacy.
practical_purpose: Teach the matched-pair technique (same spot, whole area, good light, do not tidy first), establish the before photo as the visual baseline that pairs with the audit number, and have the reader take the photo and save it in a named album.
primary_cta: Take the before photo: open a '6S Before' album, stand in one fixed spot, frame the whole audited space, take a wide and a detail shot, do not tidy first, and save them with the date. Read the chapter free in the online book.
secondary_cta: Read the chapter free online, then continue to Chapter 7 to decide what the space is actually for.
keywords: how to take before and after photos
hero_device: The Eye vs the Camera (a split showing the space soft and forgiving as the eye sees it, then sharp and honest as the camera sees it)
secondary_device: The Matched Pair (shoot the before and the future after from the same marked spot; rules: same spot, whole area, good light, do not tidy first)
definition: A before photo is not vanity and it is not for show. It is evidence. It is the visual baseline that, paired with your audit number, proves the change you are about to make actually happened.
one_idea_to_keep: The after only means something next to an honest before. Take the picture you would rather not take. It is the one that will prove, later, that you did this.
